article_title: Pathways to Quantum Science for High-School and Incoming College Students
citation: Dan-Adrian German, Rebekah Randall, Charles Pope, Michele Roberts, John Phillips. (2026). Pathways to Quantum Science for High-School and Incoming College Students. Submitted to ACM SIGCSE '27. https://homes.luddy.indiana.edu/dgerman/flc/qis/2024/final-submission.pdf
title: ZX calculus (Quantum in Pictures): graphical rewrite rules that make dualities and phase kickback accessible and yield a one-step Bernstein-Vazirani resolution
description: Quantum in Pictures, the ZX calculus "developed over 20+ years at the University of Oxford", represents gates as colored spiders whose graphical rules — copy rule and fusion — are "actually mathematical subroutines". Its "scope is wider" than the other tools: swapping spider colors changes the basis from |0⟩,|1⟩ to |+⟩,|−⟩ and reverses the roles of control and target, making phase kickback immediate and giving "a quicker and more self-contained resolution to the Bernstein-Vazirani challenge". The Snake Equation, a fundamental ZX equation, suggests quantum teleportation.
requirements: Students first work with misty states and Qiskit circuits; ZX rules and conventions are introduced once the snake-equation circuit is reached.
constraints: The article presents the ZX derivations (Figs. 10-13) as graphical proofs; empirical support for the tool comes from the cited Oxford high-schoolers study [1], not from data in this paper.
target_learning_goals: Reasoning about quantum circuits, phase kickback, Bernstein-Vazirani, and quantum teleportation
examples: The shortest possible proof for phase kickback (Fig. 10) uses the copy rule once and fusion twice; the Bernstein-Vazirani black box "reveals itself in the outputs in only one step".
